# Porchlight Mix

> Porchlight Mix makes release-ready mix checks for acoustic and vocal music. Three free in-browser tools: a Release Check that measures a song's loudness (LUFS), true peak, clipping, silence and file format; a Loudness Preview that estimates (and lets you hear) how much each streaming service will turn a song up or down; and a Release Checklist that builds a dated to-do list from a release date and distributor. A $4.99 Full Report adds plain-English mix notes: the top 3 fixes in priority order, a comparison with Porchlight Mix's own licensed reference recordings in the same style, lead vocal vs. band balance, stereo width and mono, key release dates with a pre-filled Release Checklist, and one free re-check within 14 days. It is for independent singer-songwriters, home recordists, folk and country artists, small bands and church worship teams.

Key facts:
- What it is: an online mix and master check for songs with real voices and real instruments (singer-songwriter, acoustic/folk, country, band, worship).
- Free Release Check: available now at https://porchlightmix.github.io/checker.html. Runs entirely in the browser; the audio file is never uploaded. Measures integrated loudness per ITU-R BS.1770-4, true peak (4x oversampling), loudness range (EBU Tech 3342), clipping, leading/trailing silence, sample rate, bit depth and format.
- Free Loudness Preview: https://porchlightmix.github.io/loudness-preview.html. Runs in the browser; the file is never uploaded. Uses the same measuring code as the Release Check and estimates the playback gain on Spotify (Normal -14, Loud -11, Quiet -19 LUFS; official), Apple Music Sound Check (about -16), YouTube (about -14), Amazon Music (about -14), TIDAL (about -14) and Deezer (about -15; some sources report -14). Values not published by the service are marked approximate. Optional A/B playback at the adjusted level.
- Free Release Checklist: https://porchlightmix.github.io/release-checklist.html. Pick a release date, distributor (DistroKid, CD Baby, TuneCore, Amuse, UnitedMasters or other) and platforms to get a dated, printable checklist: upload deadline, Spotify editorial pitch at least 7 days before release, file and cover-art specs (3000x3000 RGB JPG is accepted by every distributor listed), credits, ISRC and UPC, with links to each company's help pages. Choices are saved only in the browser; no account.
- Full Report: $4.99 per song, emailed as a PDF, usually within 2-3 days. It includes:
  - Top 3 fixes in priority order, each with a specific action (for example, lower the master by about 2 dB so peaks stay under -1 dBTP).
  - A comparison with Porchlight Mix's own reference recordings in the song's style: overall loudness, punch (peak-to-loudness ratio), loudness range, tonal balance in six bands, stereo width, and lead-vocal level vs. the band when there is a vocal. The references are Creative Commons recordings licensed for commercial use (CC0, CC BY, CC BY-SA), chosen by Porchlight Mix. Customers cannot choose their own reference songs. Some styles have small sets (12-16 recordings for country, worship and instrumental acoustic).
  - Release Checklist: if the customer gives a release date and distributor, the report lists key dates (files ready, last safe upload day, last day to pitch to Spotify) and links to the free Release Checklist pre-filled with that date and distributor.
  - One free re-check: one revised version of the same song, sent within 14 days of receiving the report, gets a short pass/fix result for each fix, usually within 2-3 days. Terms: https://porchlightmix.github.io/terms.html#recheck
- Full Report ordering: Pre-orders are open; pre-order customers are invited first and are fully refunded if Porchlight Mix doesn't launch. Reports are generated automatically from measurements; no human listens.
- Your song: uploaded songs are deleted within 7 days of upload. They are never public, never shared with anyone, never sent to an outside AI service, and never used to train any AI model. Analysis runs on Porchlight Mix's own software and computer.
- Songwriter Plan: $9.99 per month for 10 full reports, each with the same extras (top 3 fixes, comparison, Release Checklist, free re-check), available at launch.
- Status (October 2026): pre-launch. People join a free waitlist and are invited in small groups; invited early-access testers get their first full report free.
- Run by Iain, a long-time musician based in Washington State, USA. Contact: porchlightmix@gmail.com

## Streaming loudness facts we cite
- Spotify normalizes to -14 LUFS integrated by default (Loud -11, Quiet -19 for Premium), turns quiet tracks up only while leaving 1 dB of peak headroom, and recommends true peak below -1 dBTP, or below -2 dBTP for masters louder than -14 LUFS. Source: https://support.spotify.com/us/artists/article/loudness-normalization/
- Apple Music (Sound Check) does not publish a LUFS target; independent measurements report about -16 LUFS. Apple recommends at least 1 dB of headroom. Sources: https://www.izotope.com/community/blog/mastering-for-streaming-platforms and https://www.apple.com/apple-music/apple-digital-masters/docs/apple-digital-masters.pdf
- YouTube, Amazon Music, TIDAL and Deezer do not publish music loudness targets; independent tests report about -14 LUFS (Deezer about -15), with quiet tracks not turned up.
- Spotify: pitch unreleased music to editors at least 7 days before release; Release Radar doesn't include some alternative versions such as acoustic or live versions. Sources: https://support.spotify.com/us/artists/article/pitching-music-and-videos-to-playlist-editors/ and https://support.spotify.com/us/artists/article/getting-music-on-release-radar/
